question: Who among the following founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara, called Nagalapuram, after his mother?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Deva Raya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Krishna Deva Raya** was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire who reigned from 1509 to 1529.
 
• He founded the suburban township of **Nagalapuram** in honor of his mother, Nagala Devi.
 
• Krishna Deva Raya was known for his administrative prowess, military strength, and contributions to art, culture, and architecture in South India.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire flourished under his rule, becoming a major center for trade, culture, and religion.
 
• He also authored the Telugu literary work **Amuktamalyada**, showcasing his deep interest in literature and spirituality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, established in 1336, was one of the most significant South Indian empires, known for its contributions to art, architecture, and economy.
 
• It served as a bulwark against Islamic invasions in South India and fostered a synthesis of Hindu culture and traditions.
 
• Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Krishna Deva Raya's Achievements:**
 
 
• He expanded the empire's territory through military campaigns, including victories over the Bahmani Sultanate and the Gajapati rulers of Odisha.
 
• His reign marked a golden age of prosperity, with advancements in trade, agriculture, and irrigation systems.
 
• He patronized several temples, including the famous Virupaksha Temple in Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Amuktamalyada:**
 
 
• Written in Telugu, Amuktamalyada is a poetic work by Krishna Deva Raya that narrates the story of the Tamil saint Andal.
 
• The text reflects his deep devotion to Lord Vishnu and his intellectual engagement with literature and spiritual philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Nagalapuram:**
 
 
• Nagalapuram, named after Nagala Devi (Krishna Deva Raya's mother), is located in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The town showcases the architectural and cultural advancements of the Vijayanagara Empire.
